title: No way to select expanded disclosure widgets and dialogs by state
title_original: Add new selectors and move some existing selectors out of experimental
text_original:
- Add `:open` and `:muted`
- Recognize `:autofill`, `:buffering`, `:fullscreen`, `:picture-in-picture`, `:popover-open`, `:seeking`, `:stalled`, and `:volume-locked`.
- Move various existing pseudo-classes out of experimental status.
text_rewritten:
Our documentation tooling walks saved HTML that contains <details> and <dialog> elements and needs to pick out the ones that are currently expanded. The CSS Level 4 state pseudo-class for exactly that, :open, is refused as an unsupported pseudo-class, and because the rejection aborts the whole pattern we fall back on the attribute test [open]. That fallback is wrong: generated markup carries an open attribute on plenty of unrelated elements, and they get selected too.

Please support :open so that it selects exactly the disclosure and dialog elements that are in the expanded state. It has to work on its own, narrowed to one element type (details:open, dialog:open), and nested inside :not() and :is() like any other state pseudo-class. Attribute-presence selectors such as [open] must keep their current, broader meaning.
body:
Our documentation tooling walks saved HTML that contains <details> and <dialog> elements and needs to pick out the ones that are currently expanded. The CSS Level 4 state pseudo-class for exactly that, :open, is refused as an unsupported pseudo-class, and because the rejection aborts the whole pattern we fall back on the attribute test [open]. That fallback is wrong: generated markup carries an open attribute on plenty of unrelated elements, and they get selected too.

Please support :open so that it selects exactly the disclosure and dialog elements that are in the expanded state. It has to work on its own, narrowed to one element type (details:open, dialog:open), and nested inside :not() and :is() like any other state pseudo-class. Attribute-presence selectors such as [open] must keep their current, broader meaning.
acceptance_hint: :open compiles and selects only expanded disclosure and dialog elements, composes inside :not() and :is(), and [open] still matches every element that merely carries the attribute.
